why: A bounded-copies knapsack where the capacity and the copy counts reach 10^9, so a capacity-indexed table is impossible. Recognising the special structure (every item weighs 1, so any item can replace any other) is what replaces the DP: take the most valuable types first.
hints: The usual knapsack table has capacity + 1 cells. How many is that here?
When every item weighs the same, swapping a cheap chosen item for a more valuable unchosen one never hurts. So which items should fill the knapsack?
Sort types by value descending and take min(quantity, remaining capacity) of each until the capacity runs out. O(n log n), with 64-bit totals.
pitfalls: Totals reach about 10^18; Python is fine, but in other languages use 64-bit.
Quantities can be 0 and capacity can be 0.
Do not expand copies one by one: 10^9 copies must be taken in one step.
